react_result.final_narrative_text: Four complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: disruption of one-carbon amino acid metabolism centred on the glycine–serine–threonine axis. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies KEGG:hsa00260 'Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism' as the top KEGG hit (FDR = 1.27 × 10⁻¹⁹, fold-enrichment = 689, 8 of 57 pathway members detected) and Reactome R-HSA-71291 'Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives' as the top Reactome entry (FDR = 1.37 × 10⁻²², 11 of 288 members). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA independently confirms the same KEGG entry (p = 2.12 × 10⁻⁸, 6 of 33 members), while mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis ranks the equivalent MUMM pathway first (p = 0.0021, 14/14 input compounds mapping to this module). The five driver metabolites glycine (KEGG:C00037), O-phospho-L-serine (C01005), L-threonine (C00188), L-cysteine (C00097) and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (C00021) are verified members of the KEGG hsa00260 roster via canonical annotation. Guanidoacetic acid (C00581) and L-cystathionine (C02291) extend the signal into the connected cysteine/methionine and creatine-biosynthesis sub-threads, consistent with folate-mediated one-carbon trafficking. The treatment group therefore shows a coordinated perturbation of serine-family one-carbon metabolism, with methionine salvage and transsulfuration branch points also implicated by the N¹-acetylspermidine (C00612) and niacinamide (C00153) hits in mummichog.

Methionine metabolism leading to sulfur amino acids and related disorders

react_result.final_narrative_text: Two complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on amino-acid one-carbon metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-database ORA ranks KEGG:map00260 'Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism' first with FDR 1.27 × 10⁻¹⁹ and 8 input metabolites mapping to 57 pathway members, while mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis independently ranks 'Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism' top with p = 7.56 × 10⁻⁴ and all 14 mapped compounds overlapping the pathway. The RaMP Reactome entry 'Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives' (REACT:R-HSA-71291) sits at the apex with FDR 1.37 × 10⁻²² across 288 members and 11 input hits. WikiPathways WP:WP4292 'Methionine metabolism leading to sulfur amino acids and related disorders' (FDR 5.67 × 10⁻¹³) extends the signal into cysteine and methionine sub-pathways, capturing L-cystathionine, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, sulfate, glycine and AMP as driver members. The methionine/cysteine arm is further supported by mummichog 'Methionine and cysteine metabolism' (p = 0.024). Niacinamide (nicotinamide) is captured by the mummichog vitamin B3 pathway (p = 0.049) and maps to the broad Reactome amino-acid metabolism super-pathway. Guanidinoacetic acid links the glycine/serine cluster to creatine biosynthesis, consistent with its presence in the KEGG:map00260 hit list and the SMPDB disease entries for glycine metabolism disorders.

Guanidoacetic acid (C00581) and L-cystathionine (C02291) extend the signal into the connected cysteine/methionine and creatine-biosynthesis sub-threads, consistent with folate-mediated one-carbon trafficking.
